raw: Act 2, Scene 3 — Friar Lawrence’s Cell

sentences.en: Friar Lawrence’s Cell
sentences.ko: 로런스 신부의 수도실

summary.en: Romeo asks Friar Lawrence to marry him to Juliet. The Friar agrees, hoping the marriage will end the families' hate.
summary.ko: 로미오는 로런스 신부에게 줄리엣과 결혼시켜 달라고 부탁한다. 신부는 이 결혼이 두 집안의 미움을 끝내기를 바라며 승낙한다.

raw: Enter Friar Lawrence with a basket.

sentences.en: Friar Lawrence, a Catholic priest, enters with a basket.
sentences.ko: 가톨릭 신부인 로런스 신부가 바구니를 들고 들어온다.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
The grey-ey’d morn smiles on the frowning night,
Chequering the eastern clouds with streaks of light;
And fleckled darkness like a drunkard reels
From forth day’s pathway, made by Titan’s fiery wheels
Now, ere the sun advance his burning eye,
The day to cheer, and night’s dank dew to dry,
I must upfill this osier cage of ours
With baleful weeds and precious-juiced flowers.
The earth that’s nature’s mother, is her tomb;
What is her burying grave, that is her womb:
And from her womb children of divers kind
We sucking on her natural bosom find.
Many for many virtues excellent,
None but for some, and yet all different.
O, mickle is the powerful grace that lies
In plants, herbs, stones, and their true qualities.
For naught so vile that on the earth doth live
But to the earth some special good doth give;
Nor aught so good but, strain’d from that fair use,
Revolts from true birth, stumbling on abuse.
Virtue itself turns vice being misapplied,
And vice sometime’s by action dignified.

sentences.en: The grey-eyed morning smiles on the frowning night.
sentences.ko: 회색 눈의 아침이 찌푸린 밤을 향해 미소 짓는다.

sentences.en: It marks the eastern clouds with streaks of light.
sentences.ko: 아침은 동쪽 구름에 빛의 줄기를 새긴다.

sentences.en: And darkness like a drunkard reels from the day's path.
sentences.ko: 그리고 어둠은 술 취한 사람처럼 낮의 길에서 비틀거린다.

sentences.en: That path is made by the fiery wheels of the sun god's chariot.
sentences.ko: 그 길은 태양신 마차의 불타는 바퀴가 만든 길이다.

sentences.en: Before the sun moves forward with its burning eye, I must fill this basket of ours.
sentences.ko: 태양이 타오르는 눈으로 앞으로 나아가기 전에, 나는 이 바구니를 채워야 한다.

sentences.en: I will use harmful weeds and flowers with precious juice.
sentences.ko: 나는 해로운 잡초와 귀한 즙이 있는 꽃들을 사용할 것이다.

sentences.en: The earth is nature's mother, but it is also her grave.
sentences.ko: 대지는 자연의 어머니이자 그녀의 무덤이기도 하다.

sentences.en: What is her burial place is also her womb.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 매장지는 또한 그녀의 자궁이다.

sentences.en: From her womb, we find children of many kinds.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 자궁에서 우리는 다양한 종류의 아이들을 발견한다.

sentences.en: We find them by nursing from her natural breast.
sentences.ko: 우리는 그녀의 자연적인 젖을 먹으며 그것들을 찾아낸다.

sentences.en: Many plants have many excellent powers.
sentences.ko: 많은 식물은 많은 뛰어난 능력을 가지고 있다.

sentences.en: Every one is good for something, and each is different.
sentences.ko: 모든 것이 무언가에 유용하며, 각각이 서로 다르다.

sentences.en: There is a great power in plants, herbs, and stones.
sentences.ko: 식물과 약초, 그리고 돌에는 큰 힘이 있다.

sentences.en: They have their own true qualities.
sentences.ko: 그것들은 저마다의 진정한 특성을 지닌다.

sentences.en: Nothing living on earth is so bad that it gives no good.
sentences.ko: 지구상의 살아있는 것 중 아무리 나쁜 것도 아무런 이로움이 없는 것은 없다.

sentences.en: Everything gives some special benefit to the earth.
sentences.ko: 모든 것이 대지에 특별한 혜택을 준다.

sentences.en: And nothing is so good that it cannot turn bad when it is misused.
sentences.ko: 그리고 아무리 좋은 것도 잘못 사용하면 나쁘게 변할 수 있다.

sentences.en: Good things turn into bad things when they are misused.
sentences.ko: 좋은 것들은 잘못 쓰이면 나쁜 것으로 변한다.

sentences.en: Bad things can sometimes be made honorable by their use.
sentences.ko: 나쁜 것들도 때로는 활용 방식에 따라 고귀해질 수 있다.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Within the infant rind of this weak flower
Poison hath residence, and medicine power:
For this, being smelt, with that part cheers each part;
Being tasted, slays all senses with the heart.
Two such opposed kings encamp them still
In man as well as herbs,—grace and rude will;
And where the worser is predominant,
Full soon the canker death eats up that plant.

sentences.en: Inside the small skin of this weak flower poison lives, and medicine has power.
sentences.ko: 이 약한 꽃의 작은 껍질 안에는 독이 있고, 약초는 힘을 가진다.

sentences.en: When you smell it, it refreshes every part of the body.
sentences.ko: 그것을 맡으면 몸의 모든 부분이 상쾌해진다.

sentences.en: When you taste it, it stops the heart and kills all the senses.
sentences.ko: 그것을 맛보면 심장이 멈추고 모든 감각이 죽는다.

sentences.en: Two such opposite kings still live in man as well as in herbs.
sentences.ko: 이런 두 가지 상반된 왕이 약초뿐만 아니라 인간 안에도 공존한다.

sentences.en: These are goodness and wild desire.
sentences.ko: 이것들은 선함과 거친 욕망이다.

sentences.en: And when the worse one is stronger, death quickly eats up that plant.
sentences.ko: 그리고 더 나쁜 쪽이 강해지면, 죽음이 곧 그 식물을 집어삼킨다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Good morrow, father.

sentences.en: Good morning, father.
sentences.ko: 좋은 아침입니다, 신부님.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Benedicite!
What early tongue so sweet saluteth me?
Young son, it argues a distemper’d head
So soon to bid good morrow to thy bed.
Care keeps his watch in every old man’s eye,
And where care lodges sleep will never lie;
But where unbruised youth with unstuff’d brain
Doth couch his limbs, there golden sleep doth reign.
Therefore thy earliness doth me assure
Thou art uprous’d with some distemperature;
Or if not so, then here I hit it right,
Our Romeo hath not been in bed tonight.

sentences.en: Bless you!
sentences.ko: 신의 가호가 있기를!

sentences.en: What early voice so sweet greets me?
sentences.ko: 이렇게 이른 시간에 어떤 달콤한 목소리가 나를 반기는가?

sentences.en: Young son, getting out of bed so early shows a troubled mind.
sentences.ko: 어린 아들아, 이렇게 일찍 침대에서 나오는 것은 마음이 괴롭다는 증거다.

sentences.en: Worry keeps watch in every old man's eye.
sentences.ko: 걱정은 모든 노인의 눈속에 머문다.

sentences.en: Where worry stays, sleep will never stay.
sentences.ko: 걱정이 머무는 곳에 잠은 결코 머물지 않는다.

sentences.en: But where a young man with no worries rests his body, golden sleep rules.
sentences.ko: 하지만 걱정 없는 젊은이가 몸을 뉘이는 곳에는 황금빛 잠이 지배한다.

sentences.en: Therefore your early rising tells me you are troubled by some illness.
sentences.ko: 그러므로 네가 일찍 일어난 것은 어떤 병으로 고통받고 있다는 뜻이다.

sentences.en: Or if not that, then I am right about this: our Romeo has not been in bed tonight.
sentences.ko: 아니면 그것이 아니라면, 내 말이 맞다. 우리의 로미오는 오늘 밤 침대에 있지 않았다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: That last is true; the sweeter rest was mine.

sentences.en: That last one is true; the sweeter rest was mine.
sentences.ko: 마지막 말씀이 맞습니다. 더 달콤한 휴식은 제 것이었습니다.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: God pardon sin. Wast thou with Rosaline?

sentences.en: God forgive sin!
sentences.ko: 신께서 내 죄를 용서하시길!

sentences.en: Were you with Rosaline?
sentences.ko: 로잘린과 함께 있었느냐?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
With Rosaline, my ghostly father? No.
I have forgot that name, and that name’s woe.

sentences.en: With Rosaline, my spiritual father? No.
sentences.ko: 제 영적 스승인 로잘린 말인가요? 아니요.

sentences.en: I have forgotten that name and the sadness of that name.
sentences.ko: 그 이름도, 그 이름이 주는 슬픔도 이제 잊었습니다.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: That’s my good son. But where hast thou been then?

sentences.en: That is my good son.
sentences.ko: 착한 아들이구나.

sentences.en: But where have you been then?
sentences.ko: 그럼 어디에 있었느냐?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I’ll tell thee ere thou ask it me again.
I have been feasting with mine enemy,
Where on a sudden one hath wounded me
That’s by me wounded. Both our remedies
Within thy help and holy physic lies.
I bear no hatred, blessed man; for lo,
My intercession likewise steads my foe.

sentences.en: I will tell you before you ask me again.
sentences.ko: 물으시기 전에 미리 말씀드릴게요.

sentences.en: I have been feasting with my enemy.
sentences.ko: 적과 함께 잔치를 즐기고 있었어요.

sentences.en: Suddenly, someone wounded me there.
sentences.ko: 그런데 갑자기 누군가 저를 다치게 했어요.

sentences.en: That person is also wounded by me.
sentences.ko: 그 사람도 저 때문에 상처를 입었고요.

sentences.en: Both of our remedies lie in your help and holy medicine.
sentences.ko: 우리 둘의 치료법은 신부님의 도움과 성스러운 약에 달려 있어요.

sentences.en: I bear no hatred, blessed man.
sentences.ko: 축복받은 분이여, 저는 증오심이 없어요.

sentences.en: Look, my request helps my enemy too.
sentences.ko: 보세요, 제 요청이 적에게도 도움이 될 거예요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Be plain, good son, and homely in thy drift;
Riddling confession finds but riddling shrift.

sentences.en: Be clear, good son.
sentences.ko: 똑바로 말해라, 착한 아들아.

sentences.en: Speak simply about your meaning.
sentences.ko: 네 뜻을 있는 그대로 말해라.

sentences.en: A confession in riddles gets only forgiveness in riddles.
sentences.ko: 수수께끼 같은 고백은 수수께끼 같은 용서만 받을 뿐이다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Then plainly know my heart’s dear love is set
On the fair daughter of rich Capulet.
As mine on hers, so hers is set on mine;
And all combin’d, save what thou must combine
By holy marriage. When, and where, and how
We met, we woo’d, and made exchange of vow,
I’ll tell thee as we pass; but this I pray,
That thou consent to marry us today.

sentences.en: Then I tell you clearly: I love the beautiful daughter of rich Capulet.
sentences.ko: 그럼 분명히 말씀드릴게요. 저는 부유한 캐퓰릿의 아름다운 딸을 사랑해요.

sentences.en: Just as my love is for her, her love is for me.
sentences.ko: 제가 그녀를 사랑하는 만큼, 그녀도 저를 사랑해요.

sentences.en: We are joined in every way, except the way you must join us by holy marriage.
sentences.ko: 성스러운 결혼으로 맺어지는 것 외에 모든 면에서 우리는 하나예요.

sentences.en: I will tell you the rest on the way.
sentences.ko: 가는 길에 나머지 이야기를 해드릴게요.

sentences.en: I will tell you when, where and how we met, fell in love and made our promises.
sentences.ko: 우리가 언제, 어디서, 어떻게 만나 사랑에 빠지고 약속을 했는지 말씀드릴게요.

sentences.en: But this I pray.
sentences.ko: 하지만 이것만은 빌어요.

sentences.en: Please agree to marry us today.
sentences.ko: 오늘 저희를 결혼시켜 주시기로 약속해 주세요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Holy Saint Francis! What a change is here!
Is Rosaline, that thou didst love so dear,
So soon forsaken? Young men’s love then lies
Not truly in their hearts, but in their eyes.
Jesu Maria, what a deal of brine
Hath wash’d thy sallow cheeks for Rosaline!
How much salt water thrown away in waste,
To season love, that of it doth not taste.
The sun not yet thy sighs from heaven clears,
Thy old groans yet ring in mine ancient ears.
Lo here upon thy cheek the stain doth sit
Of an old tear that is not wash’d off yet.
If ere thou wast thyself, and these woes thine,
Thou and these woes were all for Rosaline,
And art thou chang’d? Pronounce this sentence then,
Women may fall, when there’s no strength in men.

sentences.en: Holy Saint Francis!
sentences.ko: 성 프란치스코여!

sentences.en: What a change is here!
sentences.ko: 어쩜 이렇게 변했나!

sentences.en: Is Rosaline, whom you loved so dearly, so soon abandoned?
sentences.ko: 그토록 아끼던 로잘린을 벌써 버린 건가?

sentences.en: Young men's love then lies not truly in their hearts.
sentences.ko: 젊은이들의 사랑은 진심으로 마음에서 나오는 게 아니야.

sentences.en: It lies only in their eyes.
sentences.ko: 그건 단지 눈에만 머무는 거지.

sentences.en: Jesus Mary, how much salt water has washed your pale cheeks for Rosaline!
sentences.ko: 예수 마리아여, 로잘린 때문에 네 창백한 뺨에 얼마나 많은 눈물이 흘렀던가!

sentences.en: How much salt water was wasted, to season a love that does not taste like anything.
sentences.ko: 아무 맛도 없는 사랑을 위해 그 많은 눈물을 낭비하다니.

sentences.en: The sun has not yet cleared your sighs from heaven.
sentences.ko: 태양조차 하늘에 남은 네 한숨을 다 씻어내지 못했다.

sentences.en: Your old groans still ring in my old ears.
sentences.ko: 네 오래된 신음이 내 귀에도 여전히 들려.

sentences.en: Look here, the stain of an old tear is still on your cheek.
sentences.ko: 봐라, 옛 눈물 자국이 아직도 네 뺨에 남아 있어.

sentences.en: It is not washed off yet.
sentences.ko: 아직 씻겨 나가지 않았단 말이다.

sentences.en: Once you were yourself, and these sorrows were yours.
sentences.ko: 한때 너는 너 자신이었고, 이 슬픔들도 네 것이었지.

sentences.en: Then you and these sorrows were all for Rosaline.
sentences.ko: 그때 너와 이 슬픔들은 모두 로잘린을 위한 것이었다.

sentences.en: And have you changed?
sentences.ko: 그런데 이제 변했나?

sentences.en: Then repeat this saying after me.
sentences.ko: 그럼 내 말을 따라 해봐.

sentences.en: Women may fall when there is no strength in men.
sentences.ko: 남자의 힘이 없을 때 여자는 쓰러질 수도 있다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Thou chidd’st me oft for loving Rosaline.

sentences.en: You often scolded me for loving Rosaline.
sentences.ko: 로잘린을 사랑한다고 제가 꾸중을 들었잖아요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: For doting, not for loving, pupil mine.

sentences.en: For being foolishly crazy about her, not for loving her, my student.
sentences.ko: 그녀를 사랑해서가 아니라, 어리석게 미쳐 있었기 때문에 꾸짖은 거다, 나의 제자야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: And bad’st me bury love.

sentences.en: And you told me to bury love.
sentences.ko: 그리고 저보고 그 사랑을 묻어버리라고 하셨잖아요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Not in a grave
To lay one in, another out to have.

sentences.en: You do not put one person in a grave to take another out.
sentences.ko: 한 사람을 꺼내기 위해 다른 사람을 무덤에 넣는 게 아니야.

sentences.en: It is not a matter of burying one love to have another.
sentences.ko: 하나의 사랑을 묻고 다른 사랑을 얻는 문제가 아니란 말이다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I pray thee chide me not, her I love now
Doth grace for grace and love for love allow.
The other did not so.

sentences.en: Please do not scold me.
sentences.ko: 제발 꾸중하지 마세요.

sentences.en: The girl I love now returns kindness for kindness and love for love.
sentences.ko: 제가 지금 사랑하는 소녀는 친절에 친절로, 사랑에 사랑으로 답해줘요.

sentences.en: The other did not.
sentences.ko: 다른 사람은 그러지 않았어요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
O, she knew well
Thy love did read by rote, that could not spell.
But come young waverer, come go with me,
In one respect I’ll thy assistant be;
For this alliance may so happy prove,
To turn your households’ rancour to pure love.

sentences.en: She knew well that your love was like a child reciting words it cannot spell.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 네 사랑이 글자도 못 읽는 아이가 말을 읊는 것과 같다는 걸 잘 알고 있었어.

sentences.en: But come, you young man who keeps changing his mind.
sentences.ko: 하지만 이리 와라, 마음을 자꾸 바꾸는 젊은이야.

sentences.en: Come and go with me.
sentences.ko: 나와 함께 가자.

sentences.en: I will help you in one way.
sentences.ko: 내가 한 가지 방법으로 도와주마.

sentences.en: This marriage may prove very happy.
sentences.ko: 이 결혼은 아주 행복한 결실을 맺을지도 몰라.

sentences.en: It can turn your families' hatred into pure love.
sentences.ko: 가문 사이의 증오를 순수한 사랑으로 바꿀 수도 있단다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O let us hence; I stand on sudden haste.

sentences.en: Come, let us leave now.
sentences.ko: 어서요, 이제 가요.

sentences.en: I am in a great hurry.
sentences.ko: 제가 무척 급해요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.

sentences.en: Act wisely and slowly.
sentences.ko: 현명하고 신중하게 행동해라.

sentences.en: Those who run too fast often stumble.
sentences.ko: 너무 빨리 달리는 사람은 자주 넘어지는 법이다.

raw: Exeunt.
